subject: Physics
topic: Motion in a Plane: Projectiles, Relative Frames & Curvilinear Motion
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Physics Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstruction: Motion in a Plane

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Zero-Acceleration Relative Frame of Two Freely Falling Projectiles
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Particle 1: r1(t) = u1*t + 0.5*g*t^2. Particle 2: r2(t) = r2_0 + u2*t + 0.5*g*t^2. The relative position vector is r_rel(t) = r1(t) - r2(t) = -r2_0 + (u1 - u2)*t. Relative acceleration is a_rel = g - g = 0.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Ride on particle 2. Because both particles experience the identical acceleration vector g, this common acceleration cancels out completely from the relative equation of motion.
phenomenological_reconstruction.rectified_path: Seen from particle 2, particle 1 travels along an exact straight line with constant vector velocity v_rel = u1 - u2.
phenomenological_reconstruction.collision_criterion: Collision occurs if and only if the constant relative velocity vector v_rel points directly along the initial line-of-sight vector r2_0 - r1_0.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: v_rel = 0; separation distance remains strictly constant for all t
d_min = 0; collision is inevitable regardless of gravity

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Complementary Launch Angle Degeneracy & Geometric Mean Height
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Let two projectiles be launched with speed u at angles theta and 90 - theta. Ranges are R1 = (u^2 sin 2theta)/g and R2 = (u^2 sin(180 - 2theta))/g = R1. Heights are H1 = (u^2 sin^2 theta)/(2g) and H2 = (u^2 cos^2 theta)/(2g). Their product is H1*H2 = (u^4 sin^2 theta cos^2 theta)/(4 g^2) = ((u^2 2 sin theta cos theta / g) / 4)^2 = (R/4)^2 => sqrt(H1*H2) = R/4. Flight time product is T1*T2 = (2u sin theta / g)*(2u cos theta / g) = 2R/g.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Replacing theta with 90 - theta exactly swaps the horizontal and vertical velocity components: u_x <-> u_y.
phenomenological_reconstruction.root_decomposition: Because horizontal range is proportional to the product u_x * u_y, swapping them leaves range R strictly invariant.
phenomenological_reconstruction.geometric_mean: The product of apex heights isolates the product (u_x * u_y)^2, proving sqrt(H1 * H2) = R/4 is a universal invariant independent of launch angle.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: H1 = H2 = R/4, self-complementary unique maximum range
H1 -> 0, H2 -> u^2/(2g), R -> 0, product identity holds trivially

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: River Crossing Orthogonal Decoupling: Shortest Time vs Minimum Drift
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Boat velocity relative to water is v_b at angle theta to downstream bank. Velocity components: v_x = v_r + v_b cos theta, v_y = v_b sin theta. Crossing time is t = W / v_y = W / (v_b sin theta). Downstream drift is x = v_x * t = (v_r + v_b cos theta) * W / (v_b sin theta).

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: River flow is strictly parallel to the banks. The width of the river is strictly perpendicular to the banks.
phenomenological_reconstruction.shortest_time: The river flow contributes zero velocity toward the opposing bank. To minimize time t = W / v_y, the boat must direct 100% of its engine effort across the river: sin theta = 1 => theta = 90 deg.
phenomenological_reconstruction.zero_drift: To achieve zero drift, the boat's upstream component must cancel river speed exactly: v_b cos theta + v_r = 0 => cos theta = -v_r / v_b. This is physically possible if and only if v_b > v_r.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: Zero drift is impossible; boat is inevitably swept downstream
t_min = W / v_b, drift is identically zero

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Frenet-Serret Curvature Decomposition: Projectile Apex Curvature Radius
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Trajectory of projectile has velocity v(t) and acceleration a = -g j. Intrinsic acceleration components are a_t = dv/dt = (v . a) / v and a_n = sqrt(g^2 - a_t^2). Radius of curvature is rho = v^2 / a_n.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: At any point on a smooth curve, the motion can be locally modeled as circular motion with instantaneous radius rho and normal acceleration a_n.
phenomenological_reconstruction.apex_simplification: At the highest point (apex), velocity is strictly horizontal v = u cos theta, and gravity is strictly vertical g. Therefore, velocity and acceleration are mutually perpendicular: a_t = 0 and a_n = g.
phenomenological_reconstruction.apex_curvature: The apex radius of curvature is simply rho_apex = (u cos theta)^2 / g.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: rho_apex -> 0 (path sharpens into a degenerate 1D line turnaround)

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: At the highest point of an oblique projectile flight, velocity is zero because the ball momentarily stops.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If total velocity were zero at the top, which force halted the projectile's horizontal motion? Does gravity act horizontally?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Gravity acts strictly downward! Horizontal velocity u_x = u cos theta is completely untouched by gravity and continues unaffected. At the top, the speed is u cos theta > 0.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A bullet shot horizontally from a gun stays airborne longer than a dropped coin because its high speed lifts it.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Which upward force lifts the bullet in a vacuum? Both objects start with zero vertical speed and fall under g.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: No upward force exists! Horizontal motion and vertical motion decouple completely. Both the bullet and coin experience vertical acceleration -g and hit the ground at the exact same instant.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: Because launch at 30 deg and 60 deg achieve the same horizontal range, they must have the same flight time.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: The 60 deg launch reaches a much higher peak. Can an object climb higher and return in the same time if acceleration is the same constant g?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: No! Higher ascent requires longer flight time: T = 2 u sin theta / g. The 60 deg launch stays airborne longer (T_60 / T_30 = tan 60 deg = sqrt(3)), but travels slower horizontally, yielding the exact same range product.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: To cross a river in the shortest time, you should aim downstream so the current pushes you across faster.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: The current pushes you parallel to the riverbank. Does pushing you parallel help you reach the opposite bank one second sooner?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Not by a microsecond! River width is perpendicular to current. Progress across depends solely on v_boat * sin theta. Aiming perpendicular (theta = 90 deg) maximizes crossing speed.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: A car rounding a curve at constant speed of 60 km/h has zero acceleration because speedometer is steady.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: Is acceleration defined as change in speed or change in velocity? Is the direction of motion changing?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Velocity is a vector! Turning the steering wheel changes the direction of velocity, demanding a continuous inward normal acceleration a_c = v^2 / R provided by tire friction.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.student_trap: When walking forward in vertically falling rain, you should hold your umbrella vertically to block rain coming from above.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.socratic_challenge: If you hold a vertical umbrella and walk forward, into which raindrops does your body walk?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: You walk forward into the falling raindrops! In your moving reference frame, the rain appears to come diagonally from the front, so the umbrella must be tilted forward.
